messages:
Clara (Sunburst): Hey team — just finished the enterprise onboarding flow but I don't see any API keys in the console for our project `sunburst-prod`. It says "No API keys" even though I accepted the invite and completed setup. Can someone check?

Eli (Support): thanks for the ping, Clara. Sorry about that — can you confirm the org email you used to sign up and the project slug? Also, did you sign up via SSO or email invite? :wave:

Clara (Sunburst): signed up with claire@sunburst.io via Google SSO. Project slug is `sunburst-prod`. On the billing page it looks like a new account was created, but the project dropdown only shows `sunburst-test`.

Eli (Support): got it. I'll triage. @Ravi can you look at the provisioning logs for that org? Might be a mapping issue between SSO domain and project creation.

Ravi (SRE): looking now. quick note: I see a provisioning job at 1912345699 from OnboardBot. It created an API key but associated it with `proj-8f2d` under org `sunburst-<legacy>` (legacy mapping). Looks like the SSO mapping created a duplicate org entry and the UI is showing only the visible project tied to the new org.

Ravi (SRE): logs snippet: ```
provision_service INFO 2026-07-22T14:01:39Z request_id=rq_9a2c created_key id=key_28b project_id=proj-8f2d org_id=org-legacy-sunburst user=claire@sunburst.io
auth_service WARN 2026-07-22T14:01:39Z sso_domain_mismatch detected existing_org=org-sunburst_v2 mapped_org=org-legacy-sunburst
```

Eli (Support): thanks. Looks like a race between the SSO org reconciliation and the onboard flow — the key exists but lives in the legacy org. Clara, we can either rebind the key to `sunburst-prod` or reprovision a new key scoped correctly. Which do you prefer?

Clara (Sunburst): rebind is fine as long as I don't need to reconfigure anything on our side. The SDK just needs the key.

Ravi (SRE): rebind is quick. I'll move key_28b into `proj-sunburst-prod` and update project metadata. Doing that now.

OnboardBot: automated action started: rebind_key key_id=key_28b target_project=proj-sunburst-prod request_id=rq_9a2c-step2

Ravi (SRE): rebind completed. Key now shows under project `sunburst-prod`. You should see it in Console -> Projects -> sunburst-prod -> API Keys. If not, try a hard refresh. :white_check_mark:

Clara (Sunburst): I can see it now, thanks!! Quick question — why did the provisioning pick the legacy org? We want to avoid this for future seats.

Eli (Support): good question. Root cause: SSO domain had an existing legacy org record (org-legacy-sunburst) from an older invite. The launcher logic picks an existing org by domain unless a direct project mapping exists. The reconcile step that would collapse legacy->v2 org didn't finish before the key creation, so the key landed in legacy.

Maya (Sales): fyi for account teams — when onboarding enterprise customers who used older invites, we should surface the suggestion to unlink legacy orgs before provisioning, or run the manual reconcile preflight. We'll add a note to the onboarding checklist.

Ravi (SRE): follow-up actions: 1) add short delay in onboarding job to wait for org_reconcile completed flag, 2) add an idempotent reconcile call at job start, 3) run a backfill to merge other duplicates for org domain `sunburst.io`. I'll create a ticket.

Eli (Support): for immediate workaround: if you ever don't see keys, run `redwoodctl keys list --org sunburst --project sunburst-prod` (example). If keys show up in a different project, ping support and include the provisioning request id shown in console logs.

Clara (Sunburst): got it. Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround! :pray:
